html:
Roman politician who, as tribune of the plebs in 133 BCE, passed a law to share out public land among poor citizens, and was killed for it.

He came from the top of Roman society. His mother Cornelia was a daughter of Scipio Africanus. As a young officer he fought in the Third Punic War, and in the Numantine War he negotiated a treaty to save a trapped Roman army, which the Senate then rejected.

His land law limited how much public land one family could hold and gave the surplus in small plots to the poor. He pushed it through the popular assembly over the heads of the Senate, had a fellow tribune who vetoed it removed from office, and planned to pay for the scheme with the treasure of Pergamon, left to Rome by its last king.

When he stood for a second year as tribune, a mob of senators led by his cousin Scipio Nasica clubbed him and about three hundred followers to death. It was the first time political blood was spilled in Rome's assembly in centuries. His brother Gaius took up his program ten years later.
sum: Roman politician who, as tribune of the plebs in 133 BCE, passed a law to share out public land among poor citizens, and was killed for it.
